sanskrit: tām evaṃ bruvatīṃ tārāṃ tārādhipanibhānanām vālī nirbhartsayām āsa vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: To Tārā who spoke thus — she whose face resembles the lord of stars — Vālī spoke words of rebuke and said this:

sanskrit: garjato 'sya ca saṃrambhaṃ bhrātuḥ śatror viśeṣataḥ marṣayiṣyāmy ahaṃ kena kāraṇena varānane
english: "For what reason should I endure the fury and roaring of him who is both my brother and my enemy? Tell me, O lovely-faced one.

sanskrit: adharṣitānāṃ śūrāṇāṃ samareṣv anivartinām dharṣaṇāmarṣaṇaṃ bhīru maraṇād atiricyate
english: For heroes who have never been humbled, who never turn back in battle — to endure insult, O timid one, is worse than death.

sanskrit: soḍhuṃ na ca samartho 'haṃ yuddhakāmasya saṃyuge sugrīvasya ca saṃrambhaṃ hīnagrīvasya garjataḥ
english: I am incapable of enduring in combat the fury and roaring of Sugrīva, that wretched-necked one who thirsts for battle.

sanskrit: na ca kāryo viṣādas te rāghavaṃ prati matkṛte dharmajñaś ca kṛtajñaś ca kathaṃ pāpaṃ kariṣyati
english: You should not grieve on my account concerning Rāghava; how would one who knows dharma and is grateful commit sin?

sanskrit: nivartasva saha strībhiḥ kathaṃ bhūyo 'nugacchasi sauhṛdaṃ darśitaṃ tāre mayi bhaktiḥ kṛtā tvayā
english: Turn back with the women — why do you follow me further? O Tārā, your friendship toward me has been shown; your devotion has been rendered.

sanskrit: pratiyotsyāmy ahaṃ gatvā sugrīvaṃ jahi saṃbhramam darpaṃ cāsya vineṣyāmi na ca prāṇair vimokṣyate
english: I shall go and fight Sugrīva — abandon your agitation. I will crush his arrogance; he shall not escape with his life.

sanskrit: śāpitāsi mama prāṇair nivartasva jayena ca ahaṃ jitvā nivartiṣye tam alaṃ bhrātaraṃ raṇe
english: I swear by my own life — turn back. I shall return victorious after defeating that brother of mine in battle."

sanskrit: taṃ tu tārā pariṣvajya vālinaṃ priyavādinī cakāra rudatī mandaṃ dakṣiṇā sā pradakṣiṇam
english: Then Tārā, that sweet-spoken one, embraced Vālī and, weeping softly, performed the auspicious circumambulation of him.

sanskrit: tataḥ svastyayanaṃ kṛtvā mantravad vijayaiṣiṇī antaḥpuraṃ saha strībhiḥ praviṣṭā śokamohitā
english: Then, having performed the benedictory rites as prescribed by injunction, she who desired his victory entered the inner apartments together with the women, overcome with grief.

sanskrit: praviṣṭāyāṃ tu tārāyāṃ saha strībhiḥ svam ālayam nagarān niryayau kruddho mahāsarpa iva śvasan
english: When Tārā had entered her dwelling together with the women, the angry Vālī went forth from the city, hissing like a great serpent.

sanskrit: sa niḥśvasya mahāvego vālī paramaroṣaṇaḥ sarvataś cārayan dṛṣṭiṃ śatrudarśanakāṅkṣayā
english: That swift Vālī, utterly furious, cast his gaze in all directions, eager for the sight of his enemy.

sanskrit: sa dadarśa tataḥ śrīmān sugrīvaṃ hemapiṅgalam susaṃvītam avaṣṭabdhaṃ dīpyamānam ivānalam
english: Then that glorious one beheld Sugrīva — tawny as gold, well-girded, steadfast, blazing like a fire.

sanskrit: sa taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahāvīryaṃ sugrīvaṃ paryavasthitam gāḍhaṃ paridadhe vāso vālī paramaroṣaṇaḥ
english: Seeing Sugrīva of great might standing ready for battle, the utterly furious Vālī girded his garment tightly.

sanskrit: sa vālī gāḍhasaṃvīto muṣṭim udyamya vīryavān sugrīvam evābhimukho yayau yoddhuṃ kṛtakṣaṇaḥ
english: That valiant Vālī, firmly girded, raised his fist and advanced straight toward Sugrīva, resolved to do battle.

sanskrit: śliṣṭamuṣṭiṃ samudyamya saṃrabdhataram āgataḥ sugrīvo 'pi samuddiśya vālinaṃ hemamālinam
english: Sugrīva too, raising his tightly-clenched fist and coming forward with even greater fury, aimed himself at Vālī who wore a golden garland.

sanskrit: taṃ vālī krodhatāmrākṣaḥ sugrīvaṃ raṇapaṇḍitam āpatantaṃ mahāvegam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: To Sugrīva the battle-expert, who came rushing with great speed, Vālī — his eyes red with rage — spoke these words:

sanskrit: eṣa muṣṭir mayā baddho gāḍhaḥ sunihitāṅguliḥ mayā vegavimuktas te prāṇān ādāya yāsyati
english: "This fist of mine, tightly closed with fingers firmly set — when I hurl it with full force, it will depart taking your life with it."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu sugrīvaḥ kruddho vālinam abravīt tavaiva ca haran prāṇān muṣṭiḥ patatu mūrdhani
english: Thus addressed, Sugrīva in anger replied to Vālī: "Let my fist fall upon your head, bearing away your very life."

sanskrit: tāḍitas tena saṃkruddhaḥ samabhikramya vegataḥ abhavac choṇitodgārī sotpīḍa iva parvataḥ
english: Struck by him, Vālī in great fury rushed forward with speed and began to pour forth blood, like a mountain gushing with a spring.

sanskrit: sugrīveṇa tu niḥsaṃgaṃ sālam utpāṭya tejasā gātreṣv abhihato vālī vajreṇeva mahāgiriḥ
english: By Sugrīva, who with his might uprooted a sāla tree and struck Vālī across the limbs, Vālī was shaken like a great mountain struck by a thunderbolt.

sanskrit: sa tu vālī pracaritaḥ sālatāḍanavihvalaḥ gurubhārasamākrāntā sāgare naur ivābhavat
english: Vālī, assaulted and reeling from the blow of the sāla tree, became like a vessel in the ocean weighed down by a heavy load.

sanskrit: tau bhīmabalavikrāntau suparṇasamaveginau pravṛddhau ghoravapuṣau candrasūryāv ivāmbare
english: Those two, of fearsome strength and prowess, with the speed of Suparṇa, towering and terrible in form, were like the sun and moon in the sky.

sanskrit: vālinā bhagnadarpas tu sugrīvo mandavikramaḥ vālinaṃ prati sāmarṣo darśayām āsa lāghavam
english: Sugrīva, his pride shattered by Vālī and his strength failing, yet showing his agility in anger, displayed his nimbleness before Vālī.

sanskrit: tato dhanuṣi saṃdhāya śaram āśīviṣopamam rāghaveṇa mahābāṇo vālivakṣasi pātitaḥ
english: Then Rāghava, fitting to his bow an arrow like a venomous serpent, loosed that mighty shaft and drove it into the chest of Vālī.

sanskrit: vegenābhihato vālī nipapāta mahītale
english: Struck with great force, Vālī fell to the earth.

sanskrit: athokṣitaḥ śoṇitatoyavisravaiḥ supuṣpitāśoka ivāniloddhataḥ vicetano vāsavasūnur āhave prabhraṃśitendradhvajavat kṣitiṃ gataḥ
english: Then, drenched with streams of blood-water, like a blossoming aśoka tree tossed by the wind, the son of Indra — his senses fled — fell to the ground in battle like the banner of Indra cast down.

sanskrit: tataḥ śareṇābhihato rāmeṇa raṇakarkaśaḥ papāta sahasā vālī nikṛtta iva pādapaḥ
english: Then Vālī, that hardened warrior, struck by Rāma's arrow, fell suddenly like a felled tree.

sanskrit: sa bhūmau nyastasarvāṅgas taptakāñcanabhūṣaṇaḥ apatad devarājasya muktaraśmir iva dhvajaḥ
english: His whole body laid upon the earth, adorned with ornaments of refined gold, he fell like the banner of the king of gods when its ropes are loosed.

sanskrit: tasmin nipatite bhūmau haryṛṣāṇāṃ gaṇeśvare naṣṭacandram iva vyoma na vyarājata bhūtalam
english: When that lord of the host of monkeys fell to the ground, the earth ceased to shine, like the sky when the moon is lost.

sanskrit: bhūmau nipatitasyāpi tasya dehaṃ mahātmanaḥ na śrīr jahāti na prāṇā na tejo na parākramaḥ
english: Even as that great-souled one lay fallen on the earth, neither glory, nor life, nor splendour, nor heroic power departed from his body.

sanskrit: śakradattā varā mālā kāñcanī ratnabhūṣitā dadhāra harimukhyasya prāṇāṃs tejaḥ śriyaṃ ca sā
english: The excellent garland given by Śakra — golden, adorned with gems — upheld the life, the radiance, and the glory of that foremost among monkeys.

sanskrit: sa tayā mālayā vīro haimayā hariyūthapaḥ saṃdhyānugataparyantaḥ payodhara ivābhavat
english: That hero, lord of the monkey hosts, wreathed in that golden garland, its borders fringed as if with twilight hues, resembled a rain-cloud.

sanskrit: tasya mālā ca dehaś ca marmaghātī ca yaḥ śaraḥ tridheva racitā lakṣmīḥ patitasyāpi śobhate
english: His garland, his body, and the arrow that had pierced his vitals — as though the glory were fashioned in three parts — shone even in his fallen state.

sanskrit: tad astraṃ tasya vīrasya svargamārgaprabhāvanam rāmabāṇāsanakṣiptam āvahat paramāṃ gatim
english: That weapon, hurled from Rāma's bow, lighting the path to heaven for that hero, conveyed him toward the highest destiny.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā patitaṃ saṃkhye gatārciṣam ivānalam yayātim iva puṇyānte devalokāt paricyutam
english: Him thus fallen in battle — like a fire whose flames have departed, like Yayāti fallen from the celestial world when his merit was exhausted —

sanskrit: ādityam iva kālena yugānte bhuvi pātitam mahendram iva durdharṣaṃ mahendram iva duḥsaham
english: like the sun cast down to earth by time at the end of an age, like Mahendra himself impossible to assail, like Mahendra himself impossible to endure —

sanskrit: mahendraputraṃ patitaṃ vālinaṃ hemamālinam siṃhoraskaṃ mahābāhuṃ dīptāsyaṃ harilocanam lakṣmaṇānugato rāmo dadarśopasasarpa ca
english: — Vālī, son of Mahendra, fallen, wearing his golden garland, lion-chested, mighty-armed, blazing-faced, with tawny eyes — Rāma, followed by Lakṣmaṇa, beheld and approached him.

sanskrit: sa dṛṣṭvā rāghavaṃ vālī lakṣmaṇaṃ ca mahābalam abravīt praśritaṃ vākyaṃ paruṣaṃ dharmasaṃhitam
english: Seeing Rāghava and the mighty Lakṣmaṇa, Vālī spoke words that were at once respectful and harsh, yet in accord with dharma:

sanskrit: parāṅmukhavadhaṃ kṛtvā ko nu prāptas tvayā guṇaḥ yad ahaṃ yuddhasaṃrabdhas tvatkṛte nidhanaṃ gataḥ
english: "What virtue have you gained by slaying one turned away from you? For it is because of you that I, inflamed for battle, have met my death.

sanskrit: kulīnaḥ sattvasaṃpannas tejasvī caritavrataḥ rāmaḥ karuṇavedī ca prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ
english: 'Rāma is of noble lineage, endowed with virtue, radiant, faithful to his vows, compassionate, and devoted to the welfare of his subjects' —

sanskrit: sānukrośo mahotsāhaḥ samayajño dṛḍhavrataḥ iti te sarvabhūtāni kathayanti yaśo bhuvi
english: 'He is merciful, of great energy, knowing the appointed times, firm in his vows' — thus all beings speak of your fame upon this earth.

sanskrit: tān guṇān saṃpradhāryāham agryaṃ cābhijanaṃ tava tārayā pratiṣiddhaḥ san sugrīveṇa samāgataḥ
english: Weighing those virtues and your high lineage — though restrained by Tārā — I came forth to meet Sugrīva.

sanskrit: na mām anyena saṃrabdhaṃ pramattaṃ veddhum arhasi iti me buddhir utpannā babhūvādarśane tava
english: 'He should not strike me — enraged and unwary as I am — from the side of another' — such was the thought that arose in me at not seeing you openly.

sanskrit: na tvāṃ vinihatātmānaṃ dharmadhvajam adhārmikam jāne pāpasamācāraṃ tṛṇaiḥ kūpam ivāvṛtam
english: I did not know you to be this — a man of destroyed soul, bearing the banner of dharma yet unrighteous, of evil conduct, like a well covered with grass.

sanskrit: satāṃ veṣadharaṃ pāpaṃ pracchannam iva pāvakam nāhaṃ tvām abhijānāni dharmacchadmābhisaṃvṛtam
english: Bearing the guise of the virtuous yet evil, like a fire concealed — I did not recognize you, wrapped in the disguise of dharma.

sanskrit: viṣaye vā pure vā te yadā nāpakaromy aham na ca tvāṃ pratijāne 'haṃ kasmāt tvaṃ haṃsy akilbiṣam
english: When I have done you no harm in your domain or in your city, and I do not even know you, why do you slay the innocent?

sanskrit: phalamūlāśanaṃ nityaṃ vānaraṃ vanagocaram mām ihāpratiyudhyantam anyena ca samāgatam
english: I, a monkey who always subsists on fruits and roots, who roams the forest — who was here engaged in combat with another, not with you —

sanskrit: tvaṃ narādhipateḥ putraḥ pratītaḥ priyadarśanaḥ liṅgam apy asti te rājan dṛśyate dharmasaṃhitam
english: You are known as the son of a king of men, pleasing in appearance; even the mark of dharma can be seen upon you, O king.

sanskrit: kaḥ kṣatriyakule jātaḥ śrutavān naṣṭasaṃśayaḥ dharmaliṅga praticchannaḥ krūraṃ karma samācaret
english: Who, born in a kṣatriya family, learned, with doubts resolved, wearing the mark of dharma as a guise, would commit such a cruel act?

sanskrit: rāma rājakule jāto dharmavān iti viśrutaḥ abhavyo bhavyarūpeṇa kimarthaṃ paridhāvasi
english: Rāma — born in a royal lineage, renowned as righteous — why do you roam about, unworthy yet wearing a worthy form?

sanskrit: sāma dānaṃ kṣamā dharmaḥ satyaṃ dhṛtiparākramau pārthivānāṃ guṇā rājan daṇḍaś cāpy apakāriṣu
english: Conciliation, gift, forbearance, dharma, truth, steadfastness, and heroism — these are the qualities of kings, O king; and punishment too, for those who transgress.

sanskrit: vayaṃ vanacarā rāma mṛgā mūlaphalāśanāḥ eṣā prakṛtir asmākaṃ puruṣas tvaṃ nareśvaraḥ
english: We, O Rāma, are forest-dwellers, animals who eat roots and fruits — that is our nature. You are a man, a lord of men.

sanskrit: bhūmir hiraṇyaṃ rūpyaṃ ca nigrahe kāraṇāni ca tatra kas te vane lobho madīyeṣu phaleṣu vā
english: Land, gold, and silver — these are reasons for punishment. What greed of yours in the forest, or for my fruits, is there?

sanskrit: nayaś ca vinayaś cobhau nigrahānugrahāv api rājavṛttir asaṃkīrṇā na nṛpāḥ kāmavṛttayaḥ
english: Both policy and propriety, both punishment and favour — the conduct of kings is unsullied. Kings do not act by the rule of passion.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu kāmapradhānaś ca kopanaś cānavasthitaḥ rājavṛttaiś ca saṃkīrṇaḥ śarāsanaparāyaṇaḥ
english: But you are governed by passion, irascible, unstable, your royal conduct muddled, and devoted only to the bow.

sanskrit: na te 'sty apacitir dharme nārthe buddhir avasthitā indriyaiḥ kāmavṛttaḥ san kṛṣyase manujeśvara
english: You have no reverence for dharma, your mind is not fixed on what is right; enslaved by passion through the senses, you are dragged about, O lord of men.

sanskrit: hatvā bāṇena kākutstha mām ihānaparādhinam kiṃ vakṣyasi satāṃ madhye karma kṛtvā jugupsitam
english: Having slain me here with an arrow — me, the guiltless one — O Kākutstha, what will you say in the assembly of the virtuous, having committed this censurable deed?

sanskrit: rājahā brahmahā goghnaś coraḥ prāṇivadhe rataḥ nāstikaḥ parivettā ca sarve nirayagāminaḥ
english: Slayer of a king, slayer of a brahmin, killer of cows, thief, one addicted to killing living beings, an atheist, one who marries before his elder brother — all these go to hell.

sanskrit: adhāryaṃ carma me sadbhī romāṇy asthi ca varjitam abhakṣyāṇi ca māṃsāni tvadvidhair dharmacāribhiḥ
english: My hide is not to be worn by the virtuous; my hair and bones are to be avoided; my flesh is not to be eaten by those like you who practise dharma.

sanskrit: pañca pañcanakhā bhakṣyā brahmakṣatreṇa rāghava śalyakaḥ śvāvidho godhā śaśaḥ kūrmaś ca pañcamaḥ
english: Five five-clawed animals are permitted as food for brāhmaṇas and kṣatriyas, O Rāghava: the porcupine, the śvāvidha, the monitor lizard, the hare, and the tortoise as the fifth.

sanskrit: carma cāsthi ca me rājan na spṛśanti manīṣiṇaḥ abhakṣyāṇi ca māṃsāni so 'haṃ pañcanakho hataḥ
english: My hide and bones, O king, the wise do not touch, and my flesh is not to be eaten — such am I, a five-clawed animal, slain by you.

sanskrit: tvayā nāthena kākutstha na sanāthā vasuṃdharā pramadā śīlasaṃpannā dhūrtena patitā yathā
english: With you as its lord, O Kākutstha, the earth is truly without a worthy lord — like a virtuous woman fallen prey to a scoundrel.

sanskrit: śaṭho naikṛtikaḥ kṣudro mithyā praśritamānasaḥ kathaṃ daśarathena tvaṃ jātaḥ pāpo mahātmanā
english: Treacherous, deceitful, petty, false in your outward show of humility — how is it that you, a sinner, were born of the great-souled Daśaratha?

sanskrit: chinnacāritryakakṣyeṣu satāṃ dharmātivartinā tyaktadharmāṅkuśenāhaṃ nihato rāmahastinā
english: By the elephant that is Rāma — whose girths of good conduct are severed, who transgresses the dharma of the virtuous, who has cast off the goad of righteousness — I have been slain.

sanskrit: dṛśyamānas tu yudhyethā mayā yudhi nṛpātmaja adya vaivasvataṃ devaṃ paśyes tvaṃ nihato mayā
english: Had you fought openly against me in battle, O son of a king, today you would have met the god Vaivasvata, slain by my hand.

sanskrit: tvayādṛśyena tu raṇe nihato 'haṃ durāsadaḥ prasuptaḥ pannageneva naraḥ pānavaśaṃ gataḥ
english: But I, formidable as I am, have been slain in battle by you who remained unseen — like a man overpowered by drink, bitten by a snake while asleep.

sanskrit: sugrīvapriyakāmena yad ahaṃ nihatas tvayā kaṇṭhe baddhvā pradadyāṃ te 'nihataṃ rāvaṇaṃ raṇe
english: Though you have slain me for the sake of pleasing Sugrīva, I could have bound Rāvaṇa by the neck and delivered him to you unslain in battle.

sanskrit: nyastāṃ sāgaratoye vā pātāle vāpi maithilīm jānayeyaṃ tavādeśāc chvetām aśvatarīm iva
english: I would have found out for you, at your command, where Maithilī is hidden — whether in the ocean's waters or in the underworld — as one traces a white she-mule.

sanskrit: yuktaṃ yat prapnuyād rājyaṃ sugrīvaḥ svargate mayi ayuktaṃ yad adharmeṇa tvayāhaṃ nihato raṇe
english: It would be fitting that Sugrīva obtain the kingdom on my death by natural causes — but it is unfitting that I have been slain by you through unrighteousness in battle.

sanskrit: kāmam evaṃvidhaṃ lokaḥ kālane viniyujyate kṣamaṃ ced bhavatā prāptam uttaraṃ sādhu cintyatām
english: Let the world be thus disposed by time as it will — if indeed you have a fitting response, let it be well considered."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā pariśuṣkavaktraḥ śarābhighātād vyathito mahātmā samīkṣya rāmaṃ ravisaṃnikāśaṃ tūṣṇīṃ babhūvāmararājasūnuḥ
english: Having spoken thus, his mouth parched, the great-souled son of the king of the immortals — tormented by the wound of the arrow — gazed upon Rāma who blazed like the sun, and fell silent.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ praśritaṃ vākyaṃ dharmārthasahitaṃ hitam paruṣaṃ vālinā rāmo nihatena vicetasā
english: Thus addressed with words at once respectful, grounded in dharma and good counsel, yet harsh — words spoken by the stricken and senseless Vālī — Rāma replied.

sanskrit: taṃ niṣprabham ivādityaṃ muktatoyam ivāmbudam uktavākyaṃ hariśreṣṭham upaśāntam ivānalam
english: To that foremost of monkeys who had spoken his words — like the sun bereft of radiance, like a cloud that has released its water, like a fire that has subsided —

sanskrit: dharmārthaguṇasaṃpannaṃ harīśvaram anuttamam adhikṣiptas tadā rāmaḥ paścād vālinam abravīt
english: — endowed with the qualities of dharma and statecraft, that peerless lord of monkeys, by whom Rāma had been rebuked — Rāma then spoke to Vālī:

sanskrit: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca samayaṃ cāpi laukikam avijñāya kathaṃ bālyān mām ihādya vigarhase
english: "Without understanding dharma, artha, kāma, and worldly convention, how do you in your childishness rebuke me here today?

sanskrit: apṛṣṭvā buddhisaṃpannān vṛddhān ācāryasaṃmatān saumya vānaracāpalyāt tvaṃ māṃ vaktum ihecchasi
english: Without consulting the wise elders honoured by teachers, O gentle one, you wish to speak against me here out of mere monkey frivolity.

sanskrit: ikṣvākūṇām iyaṃ bhūmiḥ saśailavanakānanā mṛgapakṣimanuṣyāṇāṃ nigrahānugrahāv api
english: This entire earth with its mountains, forests, and groves — and the power of punishment and favour over animals, birds, and men alike — belongs to the Ikṣvākus.

sanskrit: tāṃ pālayati dharmātmā bharataḥ satyavāg ṛjuḥ dharmakāmārthatattvajño nigrahānugrahe rataḥ
english: That earth is governed by the righteous-souled Bharata — truthful, upright, knowing the true nature of dharma, kāma, and artha, devoted to punishment and favour alike.

sanskrit: nayaś ca vinayaś cobhau yasmin satyaṃ ca susthitam vikramaś ca yathā dṛṣṭaḥ sa rājā deśakālavit
english: In whom both policy and propriety, and truth too are well-established, and whose heroism has been witnessed — he is the king who knows place and time.

sanskrit: tasya dharmakṛtādeśā vayam anye ca pārthivaḥ carāmo vasudhāṃ kṛtsnāṃ dharmasaṃtānam icchavaḥ
english: Acting on his orders established in dharma, we and the other kings roam the entire earth, desiring the perpetuation of righteousness.

sanskrit: tasmin nṛpatiśārdūla bharate dharmavatsale pālayaty akhilāṃ bhūmiṃ kaś cared dharmanigraham
english: While that tiger among kings, Bharata — devoted to dharma — governs the entire earth, who could transgress the bounds of righteous rule?

sanskrit: te vayaṃ mārgavibhraṣṭaṃ svadharme parame sthitāḥ bharatājñāṃ puraskṛtam nigṛhṇīmo yathāvidhi
english: We, established in our highest dharma, placing Bharata's command foremost, restrain those who have strayed from the right path, according to due procedure.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu saṃkliṣṭadharmā ca karmaṇā ca vigarhitaḥ kāmatantrapradhānaś ca na sthito rājavartmani
english: But you, your dharma sullied, censured by your deeds, governed by the rule of passion — you have not stood on the path of kingship.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitā caiva yaś ca vidyāṃ prayacchati trayas te pitaro jñeyā dharme ca pathi vartinaḥ
english: An elder brother, a father, and one who confers knowledge — these three are to be known as fathers; and they who walk the path of dharma.

sanskrit: yavīyān ātmanaḥ putraḥ śiṣyaś cāpi guṇoditaḥ putravat te trayaś cintyā dharmaś ced atra kāraṇam
english: A younger brother, one's own son, and a pupil endowed with virtues — these three are to be thought of as sons, if dharma is the governing principle here.

sanskrit: sūkṣmaḥ paramadurjñeyaḥ satāṃ dharmaḥ plavaṃgama hṛdisthaḥ sarvabhūtānām ātmā veda śubhāśubham
english: The dharma of the virtuous is subtle and supremely difficult to know, O leaper; dwelling in the heart, the ātman of all beings knows the auspicious and the inauspicious.

sanskrit: capalaś capalaiḥ sārdhaṃ vānarair akṛtātmabhiḥ jātyandha iva jātyandhair mantrayan drakṣyase nu kim
english: Fickle as you are, deliberating with fickle monkeys of unformed selves — like one born blind deliberating with the congenitally blind — what indeed can you see?

sanskrit: ahaṃ tu vyaktatām asya vacanasya bravīmi te na hi māṃ kevalaṃ roṣāt tvaṃ vigarhitum arhasi
english: I shall make this matter clear to you. Surely you ought not to rebuke me from mere anger alone.

sanskrit: tad etat kāraṇaṃ paśya yadarthaṃ tvaṃ mayā hataḥ bhrātur vartasi bhāryāyāṃ tyaktvā dharmaṃ sanātanam
english: Observe then this reason for which you have been slain by me: you cohabit with your brother's wife, having abandoned the eternal law of dharma.

sanskrit: asya tvaṃ dharamāṇasya sugrīvasya mahātmanaḥ rumāyāṃ vartase kāmāt snuṣāyāṃ pāpakarmakṛt
english: While the great-souled Sugrīva is still alive, you in your lust cohabit with Rumā — who is as a daughter-in-law to you — O perpetrator of evil deeds.

sanskrit: tad vyatītasya te dharmāt kāmavṛttasya vānara bhrātṛbhāryābhimarśe 'smin daṇḍo 'yaṃ pratipāditaḥ
english: Therefore, this punishment has been meted out to you — who have transgressed dharma and acted by passion — for this violation of your brother's wife, O monkey.

sanskrit: na hi dharmaviruddhasya lokavṛttād apeyuṣaḥ daṇḍād anyatra paśyāmi nigrahaṃ hariyūthapa
english: For one who has acted contrary to dharma and strayed from worldly convention, I see no restraint other than punishment, O lord of monkey hosts.

sanskrit: aurasīṃ bhaginīṃ vāpi bhāryāṃ vāpy anujasya yaḥ pracareta naraḥ kāmāt tasya daṇḍo vadhaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: A man who from lust makes advances upon his own natural sister, or upon the wife of his younger brother — for him death is prescribed as the punishment.

sanskrit: bharatas tu mahīpālo vayaṃ tv ādeśavartinaḥ tvaṃ ca dharmād atikrāntaḥ kathaṃ śakyam upekṣitum
english: Bharata is the sovereign of the earth; we act on his command; and you have transgressed dharma — how could this be overlooked?

sanskrit: gurudharmavyatikrāntaṃ prājño dharmeṇa pālayan bharataḥ kāmavṛttānāṃ nigrahe paryavasthitaḥ
english: The wise Bharata, governing righteously those who transgress the dharma of their superiors, is established in the restraint of those who act by passion.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu bharatādeśaṃ vidhiṃ kṛtvā harīśvara tvadvidhān bhinnamaryādān niyantuṃ paryavasthitāḥ
english: And we, O lord of monkeys, making Bharata's command our rule, are established in the restraint of those like you who have broken the boundaries of propriety.

sanskrit: sugrīveṇa ca me sakhyaṃ lakṣmaṇena yathā tathā dārarājyanimittaṃ ca niḥśreyasi rataḥ sa me
english: My friendship with Sugrīva is the same as with Lakṣmaṇa; and he who is devoted to highest good — his cause concerning wife and kingdom is mine as well.

sanskrit: pratijñā ca mayā dattā tadā vānarasaṃnidhau pratijñā ca kathaṃ śakyā madvidhenānavekṣitum
english: And a pledge was given by me then in the presence of the monkeys — how could one such as I leave a pledge unregarded?

sanskrit: tad ebhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarvair mahadbhir dharmasaṃhitaiḥ śāsanaṃ tava yad yuktaṃ tad bhavān anumanyatām
english: Therefore, by all these reasons, great and in accord with dharma, let you accept that which is a fitting chastisement for you.

sanskrit: sarvathā dharma ity eva draṣṭavyas tava nigrahaḥ vayasyasyopakartavyaṃ dharmam evānupaśyatā
english: In every way, your restraint is to be seen as dharma itself; and to one who looks upon dharma as supreme, it is a service to a friend.

sanskrit: rājabhir dhṛtadaṇḍās tu kṛtvā pāpāni mānavāḥ nirmalāḥ svargam āyānti santaḥ sukṛtino yathā
english: Men who have committed sins and been punished by kings come forth purified and reach heaven, like the virtuous who have performed meritorious deeds.

sanskrit: āryeṇa mama māndhātrā vyasanaṃ ghoram īpsitam śramaṇena kṛte pāpe yathā pāpaṃ kṛtaṃ tvayā
english: By the noble Māndhātṛ of mine, a grievous calamity was once sought — just as the sin was committed by an ascetic in that case, so the sin has been committed by you.

sanskrit: anyair api kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ pramattair vasudhādhipaiḥ prāyaścittaṃ ca kurvanti tena tac chāmyate rajaḥ
english: Even sins committed by other heedless sovereigns — they perform atonement for them, and by that the taint is quenched.

sanskrit: tad alaṃ paritāpena dharmataḥ parikalpitaḥ vadho vānaraśārdūla na vayaṃ svavaśe sthitāḥ
english: Therefore, enough of anguish — this death has been ordained according to dharma, O tiger among monkeys; we do not act by our own will.

sanskrit: vāgurābhiś ca pāśaiś ca kūṭaiś ca vividhair narāḥ praticchannāś ca dṛśyāś ca gṛhṇanti subahūn mṛgān pradhāvitān vā vitrastān visrabdhān ativiṣṭhitān
english: With snares, nooses, and various traps, both hidden and visible, men take very many animals — whether running, frightened, calm, or standing still.

sanskrit: pramattān apramattān vā narā māṃsārthino bhṛśam vidhyanti vimukhāṃś cāpi na ca doṣo 'tra vidyate
english: Men seeking meat strike animals forcefully whether they are heedless or heedful, and even those with their backs turned — and there is no fault in this.

sanskrit: yānti rājarṣayaś cātra mṛgayāṃ dharmakovidāḥ tasmāt tvaṃ nihato yuddhe mayā bāṇena vānara ayudhyan pratiyudhyan vā yasmāc chākhāmṛgo hy asi
english: Royal sages too skilled in dharma go hunting here. Therefore you, O monkey, have been slain in battle by me with an arrow — whether you fought back or not — for you are a tree-dwelling animal.

sanskrit: durlabhasya ca dharmasya jīvitasya śubhasya ca rājāno vānaraśreṣṭha pradātāro na saṃśayaḥ
english: Of the rare gift of dharma and of auspicious life, O foremost of monkeys, kings are the givers — there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tān na hiṃsyān na cākrośen nākṣipen nāpriyaṃ vadet devā mānuṣarūpeṇa caranty ete mahītale
english: One should not injure them, nor revile them, nor offend them, nor speak unpleasant words to them — these kings walk the earth in human form as gods.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu dharmam avijñāya kevalaṃ roṣam āsthitaḥ pradūṣayasi māṃ dharme pitṛpaitāmahe sthitam
english: But you, not knowing dharma, clinging to mere rage, seek to sully me — who am established in the dharma inherited from my fathers and forefathers."

sanskrit: evam uktas tu rāmeṇa vālī pravyathito bhṛśam pratyuvāca tato rāmaṃ prāñjalir vānareśvaraḥ
english: Thus addressed by Rāma, Vālī, greatly pained, then replied to Rāma with joined palms — that lord of monkeys:

sanskrit: yat tvam āttha naraśreṣṭha tad evaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ prativaktuṃ prakṛṣṭe hi nāpakṛṣṭas tu śaknuyāt
english: "What you have said, O best of men — it is indeed so; there is no doubt in this. Against the exalted, the lowly is not capable of reply.

sanskrit: yad ayuktaṃ mayā pūrvaṃ pramādād vākyam apriyam tatrāpi khalu me doṣaṃ kartuṃ nārhasi rāghava
english: Whatever unbecoming and unpleasant word I spoke before through heedlessness — even for that you should not find fault with me, O Rāghava.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi dṛṣṭārthatattvajñaḥ prajānāṃ ca hite rataḥ kāryakāraṇasiddhau te prasannā buddhir avyayā
english: For you are the knower of the true nature of things that are seen, devoted to the welfare of your subjects; your imperishable intellect is clear in determining cause and effect.

sanskrit: mām apy avagataṃ dharmād vyatikrāntapuraskṛtam dharmasaṃhitayā vācā dharmajña paripālaya
english: Me too — who am recognized as one who has placed transgression of dharma foremost — protect with words in accord with dharma, O knower of dharma.

sanskrit: bāṣpasaṃruddhakaṇṭhas tu vālī sārtaravaḥ śanaiḥ uvāca rāmaṃ saṃprekṣya paṅkalagna iva dvipaḥ
english: Then Vālī, his throat choked with tears, in a voice full of grief and sorrow, gazing at Rāma softly spoke — like an elephant mired in mud:

sanskrit: na tv ātmānam ahaṃ śoce na tārāṃ nāpi bāndhavān yathā putraṃ guṇaśreṣṭham aṅgadaṃ kanakāṅgadam
english: "It is not for myself that I grieve, nor for Tārā, nor for my kinsmen — but for my son Aṅgada, golden-limbed, foremost in virtues.

sanskrit: sa mamādarśanād dīno bālyāt prabhṛti lālitaḥ taṭāka iva pītāmbur upaśoṣaṃ gamiṣyati
english: He who, cherished from his very childhood, will be wretched at not seeing me — like a pool whose waters have been drunk, he will wither away.

sanskrit: sugrīve cāṅgade caiva vidhatsva matim uttamām tvaṃ hi śāstā ca goptā ca kāryākāryavidhau sthitaḥ
english: Bestow your highest regard upon both Sugrīva and Aṅgada — for you are the chastener and the protector, established in the rule of what should and should not be done.

sanskrit: yā te narapate vṛttir bharate lakṣmaṇe ca yā sugrīve cāṅgade rājaṃs tāṃ cintayitum arhasi
english: The same conduct that you observe, O lord of men, toward Bharata and Lakṣmaṇa — that same conduct toward Sugrīva and Aṅgada, O king, you should think fit to show.

sanskrit: maddoṣakṛtadoṣāṃ tāṃ yathā tārāṃ tapasvinīm sugrīvo nāvamanyeta tathāvasthātum arhasi
english: You should conduct yourself in such a way that Sugrīva does not despise that afflicted Tārā — blameless on her own account yet tainted by my fault.

sanskrit: tvayā hy anugṛhītena śakyaṃ rājyam upāsitum tvadvaśe vartamānena tava cittānuvartinā
english: For one favoured by you, walking under your sway and following your will, the kingdom can be enjoyed in peace."

sanskrit: sa tam āśvāsayad rāmo vālinaṃ vyaktadarśanam
english: Rāma then consoled Vālī, who was now clear of vision.

sanskrit: na vayaṃ bhavatā cintyā nāpy ātmā harisattama vayaṃ bhavadviśeṣeṇa dharmataḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ
english: "Neither should you be anxious about us, nor about yourself, O best of monkeys — we have acted with special regard for you, our resolve established in dharma.

sanskrit: daṇḍye yaḥ pātayed daṇḍaṃ daṇḍyo yaś cāpi daṇḍyate kāryakāraṇasiddhārthāv ubhau tau nāvasīdataḥ
english: He who metes out punishment to one deserving punishment, and he who deserves it and is punished — both, their purpose of cause and effect accomplished, do not fall into disgrace.

sanskrit: tad bhavān daṇḍasaṃyogād asmād vigatakalmaṣaḥ gataḥ svāṃ prakṛtiṃ dharmyāṃ dharmadṛṣṭtena vartmanā
english: Therefore you, through this contact with punishment, freed from taint, have returned to your own righteous nature, walking the path as seen by dharma.

sanskrit: sa tasya vākyaṃ madhuraṃ mahātmanaḥ samāhitaṃ dharmapathānuvartinaḥ niśamya rāmasya raṇāvamardino vacaḥ suyuktaṃ nijagāda vānaraḥ
english: Hearing those sweet, collected words of the great-souled Rāma — who treads the path of dharma, who crushes the arrogant in battle — those well-reasoned words, the monkey replied:

sanskrit: śarābhitaptena vicetasā mayā pradūṣitas tvaṃ yad ajānatā prabho idaṃ mahendropamabhīmavikrama prasāditas tvaṃ kṣama me mahīśvara
english: "O lord, whatever offensive words I, scorched by the arrow and out of my senses, not knowing, spoke against you — for this, O one comparable to Mahendra in fearsome prowess, be pleased and forgive me, O lord of the earth."
